units.function: CLI unit/parity tests for Secret declaration filters, inline Agent-env migration to references, provider bootstrap diagnostics, provider discovery/import, metadata/rotation/usage/access-event and deletion routes.
units.dependencyDirection: The Vitest suite uses shared Agent/CompanySecret types, CLI config schema, a secrets doctor check and Secret command helpers. Pure migration logic is tested alongside fetch-stubbed API routing; no real vault or encryption provider is contacted.
units.keyDataModels: Company/Agent/user-scoped Secret metadata, managed mode/provider/external reference/provider config/version/creator/resolution/rotation/deletion fields; Agent env plain or secret_ref bindings; provider config, remote discovery/import and access events.
units.lifecycle: Select declaration scopes; detect sensitive inline Agent environment values; match or create migration Secret names; replace plaintext with latest-version references; verify AWS provider bootstrap via non-secret deployment/KMS/profile settings; preview/import remote Secrets; update/rotate/inspect usage/access/delete Secret metadata.
units.testAssessment: Focused Vitest passed 8/8 tests on 2026-08-19 and CLI no-emit TypeScript passed. It meaningfully proves migrated output drops plaintext, secret_ref is not read as plain, provider preview/health/usage/access routes exist and AWS root credentials are discouraged. It omits real encryption/vault behavior, migration transaction/rollback, value transport safety, name collisions, authorization, redaction, provider failures, version pinning/rotation propagation and deletion dependencies.
units.designRationale: Separate Secret metadata/references from values, support local and external providers behind configurations, make discovery/import previewable and migrate legacy inline credentials without retaining plaintext in Agent configuration.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs vendor-neutral, self-hosted/cloud Secret handling where the control plane never carries unnecessary credentials or private sessions, principals receive least-privilege runtime references, and every resolution/rotation/use is governed and auditable.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT SecretPort/provider abstraction, preview-before-import, access/usage projections, strict plaintext-to-reference migration and default credential-chain guidance. Use collision-resistant opaque Secret IDs, explicit version/rotation policy, transactional migration and secure interactive/stdin/file-descriptor value ingestion. Keep Secret values in customer execution/data nodes where configured and never encode them into Connector or responsibility events.
units.responsibilityConflict: Secret access events are necessary evidence but do not alone prove authorized purpose. Each runtime resolution must bind the exact Work/Agent/runtime, responsible human, permission/data contract, provider/version and result without revealing the value; user-specific Secrets must not silently transfer with Work or Agent reassignment.

2026-08-19 focused Vitest: 1 file and 8 tests passed
securityFindings: Critical adoption blocker: the tested rotate command accepts the new Secret through `--value`, which can leak through shell history, process listings, terminal recording and diagnostic capture; Company OS must prohibit this interface.
Migration naming uses a short Agent-id prefix plus normalized environment key; collision and rename behavior are untested and names must not be identity/security keys.

Sensitive-key detection can miss unconventional names or classify benign values; migration needs policy-driven classification, preview, explicit confirmation and a no-plaintext postcondition over all persisted/logged artifacts.
The test proves output no longer contains one plaintext fixture but does not inspect requests, logs, errors, memory lifetime, backups or old configuration revisions for residual Secret values.

Provider discovery/import/config/health requests use generic JSON and fixed auth; external namespace allowlists, credential scope, cross-company isolation, SSRF, pagination/rate limits and partial import rollback are untested.
Using version `latest` can make execution non-reproducible and approval-substitutable; high-risk Work may need an immutable resolved version/digest recorded without exposing the value.
Secret deletion has typed confirmation in the CLI but no tested active usage/dependency block, grace period, recovery, concurrent resolution or evidence-retention behavior.
User-specific runtime Secrets raise reassignment and delegation risks; owner authority and non-transfer semantics are present in metadata but not exercised here.
